This confirms the CLAUDE.md 'Struct-by-value helpers' section and its 'Follow-ups' migration note (which cites ducklib.py:1525-1640, past the file's actual 1432-line end) are stale documentation describing an earlier architecture; the migration to `_call_lib_func` has already happened for hugeint/uhugeint/interval/decimal/varint alike. So the full struct-by-value suite -- test_bind_hugeint (835), test_bind_uhugeint (853), test_bind_interval (871), test_bind_decimal (891), and the create/get-value equivalents -- genuinely executes on windows-latest in CI, driving numbox's `_call_lib_func` (numbox/core/bindings/call.py:21-200) through its real Windows x64 branches: `_PLATFORM_WIN_X64` register-passable-size dispatch (lines 103-111, 150-158), `sret` for non-register-passable small/large structs (137-142, 183-193), and the byval/alloca-pointer path (166-171). Only the second half of the compound finding survives: /home/erik/projects/numbduck/numbduck/utils.py's macOS-only `_download_libduckdb`/`_find_standalone_libduckdb`/`_MACOS_LIBDUCKDB_SEARCH_PATHS` (lines ~22-84) are genuinely never referenced by any test (grepped test/test_ducklib.py and test/test_init.py -- no hits), and numbduck_ci.yml has no macOS/darwin leg at all. That sub-claim alone would support a narrow, low-severity finding, but it is not what TST-cover-10 as written and titled asserts as its primary defect, and it does not rescue the finding's false 'CI is Linux-only' / Windows-untested characterization. Given the finding conflates a real gap (macOS loader) with a demonstrably false one (Windows ABI, backed by a nonexistent function-name citation), and the false half is what the title foregrounds and the impact statement is built on, the finding as stated is refuted.
note: A narrower, accurate finding would be: 'numbduck/utils.py's macOS library-download/standalone-search branches (load_duckdb -> _find_standalone_libduckdb / _download_libduckdb) have zero test coverage and no CI leg exercises them' -- but that is not what TST-cover-10 claims or how it characterizes severity/impact.
